The B'-C band has FOUR verticals in a row, all read at 5x zoom: 1'(-1.00) = B1, grid 1 = B10A, 1''(1.90) = B2, grid 2 = B8A. The earlier extraction had B10A floating at '~1-2' and B1 at 'B'1-C1' with no span; B2 was missing entirely. The A-B band's floating '~1-2' B1 is the same 1.90 column (faces x=1268/1284 px).

Row-by-row sweep result, for anyone re-checking the count: row A has a beam in both bays; row B in both; row B' ONLY in the grid1-2 bay (grid2-3 returns a bare 0.808 line); row C in both; row D ONLY in the grid2-3 bay; row E only in grid2-3. The beam previously recorded as B2 D1-D2 span 3.00 does not exist — that stretch of row D carries only the dash-dot line (0.789), verified at 4x zoom with the B0 marker and the two C1 column marks visible and nothing between them. It has been deleted, and the row-D beam that does exist is now D2-D3 span 3.50 instead of the unplaced '~D2-D3'.

STILL UNPLACED (unchanged, genuinely hard): the porch archway group at the south end — B0 ~D1, B1 D1-~E1, B1' ~E1, B1' ~E3, and the B3 ~D2-E2 semicircular arch. These are drawn as a curved arc plus short stubs with no straight grid-to-grid run and no printed dimension, so they keep their '~' refs. The chamfered 45-degree wall east of grid 3 between rows C and D is the same case: the C-D band has a vertical beam only at grid 2 (grid 1 and grid 3 both return bare lines there), because the east side follows the chamfer instead.

Every beam segment carries a small local slab-top offset in parentheses next to its mark (e.g. 'B2(+0.40)') — this is the printed slab elevation relative to this floor's structural level, NOT a building-wide z-level, so it is kept as this element's 'level_m' field rather than promoted to the grid master's z_levels[] (see grid master warnings).

Column 'CA' at grid1/row B' has no footing (per หน้า17 warnings) — it is a special column landing directly on beam B1(B'-C) per this sheet's own legend note 'เสา CA เสริมพิเศษบนคาน' (special CA column reinforced atop a beam). Recorded as a column element here since this is its only appearance in the drawing set.

The grid1-2 span (row A-B, and again row B'-C) is each internally sub-divided into two rooms by an extra vertical beam (also marked 'B1' in the A-B bay; marked 'B10A' in the B'-C bay) that does NOT sit on any named or dummy grid line, and no printed sub-dimension locates it precisely within the 3.00 m bay in the available scan. Per the beam-endpoint rule this should get its own dummy grid, but inventing a pos_m with no printed basis would violate the 'never guess pos_m' rule — so these two internal beams are recorded with an approximate grid_ref ('~1-2') and reduced confidence rather than a fabricated dummy-grid coordinate, and are flagged here rather than silently dropped. The two slab bays they divide are recorded as separate slab elements either side.

The 'S1' slab bay at grid1-2 x B-B' prints two different local levels inside the same cross-hatch box (+0.40 and +0.35) — likely a sloped/drained slab rather than a transcription conflict. Both values are kept (level_m = leading value, both recorded in level_m_printed_as) rather than averaging them into a fabricated single number.

The porch/entrance zone (grid1-3, row D to E) includes a curved archway beam (marked B3, level +0.20, drawn as a semicircular arc rather than a straight grid-to-grid segment) plus two short stub beams marked B1'(+0.30) flanking it and a small stub 'B0(+0.10)' near grid1/row D. None of these sit on simple two-point grid lines — their extents are approximated (prefixed '~') at reduced confidence (0.5) rather than invented as precise grid coordinates. The full architectural detail for this porch arch would be on a Pass-3 entrance detail sheet, out of op04 scope.

Slab markers S0/S1 (plank-direction/void indicators) are recorded as element_type 'slab' with their printed local level; S1 boxes show a diagonal X pattern typically meaning a plank-laid slab bay in this drawing series (not a structural void).
